Introduction and meaning
Dowry death, moved from the homicide chapter into Chapter V. Death of a woman by burns or bodily injury, or otherwise than under normal circumstances, within 7 years of marriage, where she was subjected to dowry-related cruelty soon before her death.
In student language: BNS s. 80 is the rule on “Dowry death”. The section provides that (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called “dowry death”, and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 80 exists so that “Dowry death” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

The provision in detail
80. (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called “dowry death”, and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death

Essential ingredients
1. (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called “dowry death”, and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death

Punishment / legal consequence
Minimum 7 years, may extend to life.

Explanations
Explanation.—For the purposes of this sub-section, “dowry” shall have the same meaning as in section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961

(2) Whoever commits dowry death shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life

hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 80 (Dowry death), Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called “dowry death”, and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 80 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

learningObjectives: Master the constituent elements of dowry death under BNS s. 80.
Analyze the temporal requirement (death within seven years of marriage) and abnormal circumstances.
Understand the statutory nexus of cruelty/harassment 'soon before death' in connection with dowry demands.
Analyze the statutory presumption of dowry death under evidentiary law.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 80 defines dowry death as the death of a woman caused by burns, bodily injury, or occurring otherwise than under normal circumstances within seven years of her marriage, where it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Dowry death operates as a statutory deeming provision attributing culpable homicide liability to the husband or his relatives when an unnatural marital death occurs within seven years of marriage following proximate dowry-related cruelty or harassment.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 80 (corresponding to IPC s. 304B).

Sub-section (1): Deeming clause establishing dowry death where death occurs by burns, bodily injury, or abnormal circumstances within seven years of marriage and cruelty/harassment for dowry occurred soon before death.
Sub-section (2): Punishment — imprisonment for a term not less than seven years, which may extend to imprisonment for life.
Explanation: 'Dowry' has the same meaning as in Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
Evidentiary link: Rebuttable statutory presumption of dowry death under Section 118 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.
essentialIngredients: The death of a woman was caused by burns, bodily injury, or occurred otherwise than under normal circumstances.
The death occurred within seven years of her marriage.
Soon before her death, the woman was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband.
Such cruelty or harassment was for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 80 targets the menace of bride burning and dowry-related homicides and suicides occurring within the matrimonial home. The law establishes a severe deeming fiction: if a woman dies unnaturally within seven years of marriage and the prosecution establishes proximate harassment or cruelty relating to dowry demands ('soon before death'), the husband or relatives are legally deemed to have caused her death. The phrase 'soon before death' requires a proximate and live link between the cruelty and the fatal event, ruling out remote or stale incidents. The definition of dowry incorporates Section 2 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, encompassing any property or valuable security given or agreed to be given directly or indirectly in connection with the marriage. The minimum mandatory punishment is seven years imprisonment, extendable to imprisonment for life.
examples: Teaching example (Unnatural death within seven years): A woman dies of extensive kerosene burn injuries in her matrimonial home five years after marriage. Evidence shows persistent physical assaults and verbal threats by her husband and mother-in-law demanding a new luxury car during the months and days immediately preceding her death. All ingredients of s. 80 are established; the deemed causation applies.

Teaching example (Lack of proximate nexus): A woman commits suicide eight years after marriage following general marital discord unrelated to dowry demands. Section 80 does not apply because the death occurred outside the statutory seven-year window, though charges under s. 85 and s. 108 may be considered.
distinctions: Dowry death (s. 80) vs Cruelty (s. 85): Section 85 penalizes matrimonial cruelty independently without requiring death; Section 80 specifically penalizes unnatural deaths within seven years linked to dowry demands.

Dowry death (s. 80) vs Murder (s. 103): In murder, the prosecution must prove direct actus reus and mens rea of causing death; under s. 80, proof of unnatural death within seven years coupled with proximate dowry cruelty triggers a statutory deeming fiction of causation.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether the accused husband can escape liability under BNS s. 80 by claiming the wife committed suicide due to depression.

Rule: Under BNS s. 80(1), death occurring 'otherwise than under normal circumstances' expressly encompasses suicide, provided it occurred within seven years of marriage and was preceded soon before by dowry harassment.

Application: The marriage took place three years prior. Neighbor testimony and contemporaneous messages establish repeated demands for gold ornaments and physical abuse two weeks prior to the suicide.
Conclusion: The live nexus is established; the death constitutes dowry death under s. 80.
